public_rationale: On January 9, 2026, Hegseth signed a memo directing the Department of War to become an "AI-first" warfighting force "across all components, from front to back" (e1). The same memo's "Speed Wins" section says "the risks of not moving fast enough outweigh the risks of imperfect alignment" (e2). An AP report published February 24, 2026 says that in a January speech at SpaceX, Hegseth said he was shrugging off AI models "that won't allow you to fight wars" (e3). The signed memo falls within the contract's target period. It directs AI deployment across the whole department and names speed as a priority. That meets the contract's support condition. The claim's reference to his career is about motive, which this evidence cannot test. The grade covers his public directives only.
limitations: The evidence does not show Hegseth's motive or how he sees his career. It shows only his public directives and statements.
The memo was read from a third-party mirror because the official copy returned HTTP 403.
The January speech is known only through AP's short summary. It concerns rejecting restricted AI models, not the pace of adoption.
The packet does not show how AI ranks against Hegseth's other priorities, and it came from only two searches.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: Hegseth has made broad, rapid military AI adoption a signature, publicly championed priority of his tenure. His inner motives about his 'career' cannot be observed, so the test is whether his public directives and speeches put fast, department-wide AI deployment at the center of his agenda.
criteria.support_condition: Hegseth's own directives or speeches from around the post date push AI deployment across the whole department at maximum speed, as a headline priority.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Hegseth's record shows a cautious or low-priority approach to AI adoption, or AI is a minor item in his agenda.
